title: Direction Stack L2 Domain Profiles — Multi-Domain Support
description: L2 domain profiles are always empty because there is no UI to manage them. A domain profile is reusable across all workspaces sharing the same domain (e.g. all TypeScript projects share auth patterns, API conventions, error handling styles). This spec builds the Domain Profiles management UI inside the Direction Stack panel, the backend API for listing/writing L2 layers by domain, and wires them into spec generation so every workspace automatically picks up its domain context.

userStories.title: Backend: list all domains and read/write L2 by domain slug
userStories.description:
Extend ~/rorca/backend/src/routes/direction.ts with domain-level endpoints.

New endpoints:

GET /api/direction/domains
- Returns all distinct domain slugs that have an L2 entry in direction_layers
- Also returns domains from all registered workspace `domains` arrays (even if no L2 content yet)
- Response: { domains: Array<{ slug: string; hasContent: boolean; workspaceCount: number }> }
- Sorted alphabetically

GET /api/direction/domains/:slug
- Returns the L2 content for a domain slug
- Response: { slug, contentYaml: string | null, updatedAt: string | null }
- 200 with null contentYaml if no L2 exists yet (not 404)

PUT /api/direction/domains/:slug
- Body: { contentYaml: string }
- Upserts into direction_layers (layer=2, domain=slug, workspace_id=NULL)
- Returns { ok: true, updatedAt: string }

DELETE /api/direction/domains/:slug
- Deletes the L2 row for the domain
- Returns { ok: true }

Update GET /api/direction/synthesize to use domain slugs from the workspace's domains array when fetching L2 — if a workspace has domains: ['typescript', 'saas'], merge both L2 profiles (later slug wins on key conflict).
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/direction/domains returns all domain slugs with hasContent and workspaceCount
GET /api/direction/domains/:slug returns L2 YAML or null (never 404)
PUT /api/direction/domains/:slug upserts L2 row, returns updatedAt
DELETE /api/direction/domains/:slug removes the row
GET /api/direction/synthesize merges all L2 layers from workspace.domains array
cd ~/rorca/backend && npx tsc --noEmit passes

userStories.title: Direction Stack panel: Domain Profiles tab
userStories.description:
Add a 'Domains' tab to the Direction Stack panel (alongside existing L1/L2/L3 tabs).

File: ~/rorca/src/panels/DirectionStackPanel.tsx

Domains tab layout:
- Left sidebar (200px): list of all domain slugs
  - Each row: domain name + workspace count badge + green dot if has L2 content
  - '+ New Domain' button at bottom
  - Click a domain → load its L2 content on the right

- Right area: L2 content editor for selected domain
  - Header: domain slug (monospace, bold) + 'Used by X workspaces' subtitle
  - YAML editor (same CodeMirror/textarea component used for L1/L3)
  - [Save] and [Delete Domain] buttons
  - Empty state when domain has no L2 yet: 'No domain profile yet — start typing YAML below'

- New Domain form (appears when '+ New Domain' clicked):
  ```
  Domain slug: [typescript    ]
               (lowercase, hyphens ok)
  [Create]
  ```
  Validates: lowercase, alphanumeric + hyphens only. Calls PUT /api/direction/domains/:slug with empty YAML, then selects the new domain.

Workspace registration flow: when adding a workspace, the domains[] array input should autocomplete from existing domain slugs (GET /api/direction/domains).
acceptanceCriteria: Direction Stack panel has 'Domains' tab alongside L1/L2/L3
Domain list shows all slugs with workspace count and content indicator
'+ New Domain' opens inline creation form with slug validation
Selected domain shows L2 YAML editor with Save and Delete buttons
Save calls PUT /api/direction/domains/:slug and shows success state
Delete calls DELETE and removes domain from list
Empty state rendered for domains with no L2 content

userStories.title: Spec generation: show active L2 layers in Spec Forge context preview
userStories.description:
In Spec Forge, after the user selects a workspace, show which Direction Stack layers are active for that workspace — including which L2 domain profiles will be injected.

Below the workspace selector, add a small collapsible 'Context Preview' section:
```
▶ Active Direction Stack  (click to expand)
  ✓ L1 Global Brain        (populated)
  ✓ L2 typescript          (populated)
  ✓ L2 saas-api            (populated)
  ✓ L3 Project Brief       (populated)
  ✗ L4 Spec Brief          (enter brief above)
  ✗ L5 Story Annotations   (none)
```

Fetch on workspace select:
- GET /api/direction?workspaceId=&layer=1 → L1 status
- GET /api/direction/domains (+ cross-reference with workspace.domains) → L2 statuses
- GET /api/direction?workspaceId=&layer=3 → L3 status

L4 status derives from whether the brief textarea is non-empty.
L5 always shows 'none' (not yet implemented in UI).

Each row is clickable → navigates to Direction Stack panel to fill in that layer.
acceptanceCriteria: Context Preview section renders below workspace selector in Spec Forge
L1 row shows populated/empty based on GET /api/direction?layer=1
L2 rows rendered per domain in workspace.domains[], each showing populated/empty
L3 row shows populated/empty based on GET /api/direction?workspaceId=&layer=3
L4 row dynamically reflects brief textarea content
Clicking any row navigates to Direction Stack panel for that layer
Section is collapsible (collapsed by default, expands on click)
npx tsc --noEmit passes

userStories.title: Gate validation — L2 domain profiles end-to-end
userStories.description:
Full gate for the L2 Domain Profiles feature.

**Checklist (document in story notes):**
1. `cd ~/rorca/backend && npm test` — all tests pass including new domain endpoint tests
2. `npx tsc --noEmit` at ~/rorca/ root — 0 errors
3. Open Direction Stack panel → Domains tab → create 'typescript' domain profile with sample YAML
4. Create 'saas-api' domain profile with different YAML
5. Add a workspace with domains: ['typescript', 'saas-api'] → pills render correctly
6. Open Spec Forge → select that workspace → Context Preview shows L2 typescript ✓ and L2 saas-api ✓
7. Generate a spec → verify the synthesized prompt includes both L2 profiles (check backend log)
8. Test DELETE domain → removed from list and from synthesized context
9. `npm run build` — clean build
10. `git add -A && git commit -m 'feat(direction-stack): L2 domain profiles — multi-domain support'`
acceptanceCriteria: Backend domain endpoint tests pass

Domain Profiles tab functional: create, edit, delete domain profiles
